short: one edit turns a wrong total into the right one
note: A single remask edit: the run without it answers wrong, the run with it answers right. One edit, one changed token, everything else follows from it.

short: one edit repairs the function body
note: The code fails its tests without remasking and passes with it, off one replaced token.

short: one edit repairs a syntax error
note: Without remasking the extracted code does not parse; the single edit makes it valid and correct. On MBPP+ this is the pattern behind the drop in syntax errors (8 to 2 at delta=3).

short: one edit derails a correct chain
note: The mirror image: correct without remasking, wrong with it. Dream's full-context judgement replaces a token that was right.

short: one edit breaks passing code, same length
note: Same token count before and after: one token inside the function body changes, and the tests stop passing.

short: one edit breaks passing code at delta=10
note: At the loose end of the sweep, where the delta rule accepts almost everything SDAR proposes and remasking is the only check on content.

categoryLabel: Remasking moved where the answer ends
note: Without remasking this task never stops and fills the whole 256-token canvas. One remask edit puts a stop token in, and the answer ends at 52 tokens. Both are scored wrong, but this is the clearest case of remasking controlling completion.

categoryLabel: Remasking moved where the answer ends
note: The opposite direction: remasking replaces the stop token with content, so decoding continues for another seven blocks. Both versions pass.

categoryLabel: Remasking moved where the answer ends
short: code cut from 128 to 80 tokens, and it stops passing
note: Ending an answer early is not free: here the edit truncates working code and the tests fail. This is the failure mode the stop-token rule was changed to avoid, in its remaining form.
